overview.title: Overview
overview.intro: Four invented producers send synthetic crash, traffic and road segment feeds. Sikka checks each feed against one open contract, scores conformance with intervals, and ranks road segments by potential for safety improvement.
overview.producers_conforming_help: A producer conforms when at least {{threshold}} percent of its records pass every rule family. The range shows how many producers conform at the lower and at the upper end of their intervals.
overview.rules_failing_help: Rules (out of all rules evaluated) that flagged at least one record, series or file.
overview.matrix: Conformance by producer and rule family
overview.matrix_help: Share of records passing each family, with Wilson 95 percent intervals.
overview.chart_aria: Share of records passing per producer and family, with intervals
overview.score_definition: A record passes a family when no error or warning rule of that family flagged it, directly or through its station series. Informational and file level findings do not count against records. Intervals are Wilson 95 percent intervals. The overall index is the share of records that pass every family; it is always shown beside the family scores.
overview.dataset_broken: the synthetic sample feeds as received, with every catalogued fault injected at 3 percent.
overview.ranked_help: Segments with a daily traffic estimate and enough data to rank.
overview.abstained_help: Segments not ranked, each with a stated reason.
overview.top10_help: Ranked by potential for safety improvement on the feeds as received, with the 90 percent rank interval and the chance of being in the top {{k}}.

blackspots.title: Blackspots
blackspots.intro_1: Road segments ranked by potential for safety improvement
blackspots.intro_3: with rank intervals that include data quality. The ranking is a screening aid on synthetic data, not a finding about any real road.
blackspots.dataset_broken_help: The feeds as received carry every catalogued fault at 3 percent. Compare with the clean feeds to see how data quality moves the ranking.
blackspots.dataset_clean_help: The same synthetic world without injected faults.
blackspots.table_help: Rank by potential for safety improvement. The whisker is the 90 percent rank interval from {{draws}} posterior draws; the last column is the chance of being in the top {{k}}.
blackspots.map_help: Select a segment in the table or on the map. No base map tiles are loaded.
blackspots.abstained_help: These segments are listed with their reason instead of being dropped silently.
blackspots.spf_fit: Overdispersion shape k = {{k}} on {{n}} segments; McFadden pseudo R squared {{r2}}; Pearson dispersion {{pearson}}.
blackspots.capture_help: Chapman estimate of the total from two overlapping producers. It assumes independent detection, which flatters completeness.
blackspots.why_ranked: The segment had {{observed}} crashes per year against {{predicted}} expected for its traffic, length, class and lanes (ratio {{ratio}}). The prediction gets a weight of {{weight}}, so the Empirical Bayes estimate is {{eb}} per year, {{psi}} above expectation. That places it at rank {{rank}}, with a 90 percent interval from {{low}} to {{high}} and a {{p}} chance of being in the top group.
blackspots.caveat_quality: Counts in this corridor were scaled by an average undercount factor of {{factor}}.
blackspots.caveat_unresolved: Unresolved duplicate pairs on this segment: {{count}}.
blackspots.caveat_coverage: Producers expected here delivered data in {{coverage}} of the months.
blackspots.caveat_synthetic: All numbers come from the synthetic world.
blackspots.compare_text: Rank on the feeds as received: {{received}}. Rank on the clean feeds: {{clean}}.

method.title: Method and limits
method.intro: How the ranking is computed, what it assumes, and how it performed on the synthetic world against predictions written before any result existed.
method.assumption_synthetic: All data is synthetic; the world, faults and method share one author.
method.assumption_spf_form: Expected crashes follow a negative binomial safety performance function of traffic, length, class and lanes.
method.assumption_exposure: Daily traffic is estimated from one week of hourly station counts and treated as constant over five years.
method.assumption_independence: Producers detect crashes independently, which capture recapture needs.
method.assumption_matching: Duplicate reports differ by a few minutes and tens of metres; the matching parameters are stated assumptions.
method.assumption_window: The observation window is the five local calendar years 2021 to 2025.
method.terms: safety performance function, Empirical Bayes, potential for safety improvement.
method.predictions_help: Each prediction was committed before the evaluation ran. Hits and misses are both shown.
method.no_results: The evaluation has not been run in this build.
method.e3_chart: Share of planted blackspots with exposure found in the top 12, per method, with intervals
method.ranking_text: {{ranked}} segments ranked, {{abstained}} not ranked with a stated reason, intervals from {{draws}} posterior draws.
method.limit_synthetic: Every result holds for the synthetic world only.
method.limit_author: The world, the faults, the rules and the method were built by the same author, so they agree better than real data would.
method.limit_catalogue: Fault detection is measured on catalogued faults; unanticipated defects are not covered.
method.limit_spf: The synthetic crash process has the same form as the safety performance function, which favours the method.
method.limit_exposure: Traffic is constant across years and estimated from one week of counts.
method.limit_capture: Capture recapture assumes independent detection; real reporting is correlated, so completeness is overstated.
method.limit_tasking: Drone missions are for simulation and review only; real flights need the operator's own safety case and the regulator's approval.

pilot.title: Pilot path
pilot.intro: What would be needed to run Sikka on real data. This page is a proposal for discussion, not a description of any existing arrangement.
pilot.proposal: Proposal only: no entity has agreed to any of the steps below.
pilot.agreement_parties: Named data owners and a named recipient for each feed.
pilot.agreement_purpose: A stated purpose limited to road safety screening and data quality feedback.
pilot.agreement_fields: The contract fields to be shared, with prohibited fields excluded at source.
pilot.agreement_frequency: Delivery frequency and the expected delay for late records.
pilot.agreement_retention: Retention periods and deletion on request.
pilot.agreement_security: Storage, access control and encryption in transit and at rest.
pilot.agreement_exit: How the agreement ends and what happens to derived data.
pilot.privacy_dpia: A data protection impact assessment before any real record is processed.
pilot.privacy_minimise: Data minimisation: no names, identity numbers, phone numbers, plates or narratives.
pilot.privacy_quarantine: Automatic quarantine of any personal field, with no values displayed or stored.
pilot.privacy_access: Role based access and logging of every access to record level data.
pilot.privacy_audit: Periodic audit of quarantine logs and access logs.
pilot.roles_owner: Contract owner: approves versions and changes.
pilot.roles_steward: Data steward per producer: answers conformance findings.
pilot.roles_analyst: Analyst: runs rankings and documents decisions.
pilot.roles_reviewer: Independent reviewer: checks method, results and limitations.
pilot.contract: What would change in the contract
pilot.contract_identifiers: Shared crash identifiers between producers, so matching becomes exact.
pilot.contract_segments: An agreed segment registry with stable identifiers and validity dates.
pilot.contract_severity: A single agreed severity definition, with mapping tables for legacy codes.
pilot.contract_exposure: Continuous station counts with documented calibration.
pilot.contract_version: A governance process for major and minor contract versions.
pilot.step_one: Review the contract with producers and agree version 1.
pilot.step_two: Run conformance checks on a historical extract with privacy controls in place.
pilot.step_three: Compare rankings with existing engineering judgement before any use.
pilot.step_four: Publish an evaluation with limitations before any operational decision.

tasking.title: Tasking
tasking.intro_1: Where should a survey drone look? Segments whose top 12 membership is most uncertain carry the most
tasking.intro_2: (the probability mass p times 1 minus p, per kilometre surveyed). Missions follow corridors within the drone profile.
tasking.disclaimer: For simulation and review only; real flights need the operator's own safety case and the regulator's approval.
tasking.profile: Profile: {{endurance}} minutes endurance, {{speed}} m/s, {{reserve}} percent reserve, {{altitude}} m altitude, so {{usable}} s of usable flight.
tasking.refused: Refused because a single segment exceeds the profile: {{segments}}.
tasking.voi_help: Highest first. Only ranked segments have a value; the top 30 are shown.
tasking.comparison_help: The same number of missions planned three ways on the demo ranking: by value of information, in random order, and greedily by crash count.
tasking.e5_chart: Relative reduction of top 12 uncertainty per strategy, mean over seeds with intervals
